data.long_meaning: Inessa is derived from the Hebrew word ‘iness’, meaning ‘my grace’ or ‘my gracious one’. The name is also associated with the Greek goddess Hera, symbolizing nobility and purity. The name Inessa carries the meaning “Noble, Pure” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Inessa usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, pure and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Inessa of Kiev, daughter of Prince Sviatoslav I of Kiev, was a princess of the Rurik Dynasty in Kievan Rus. She was betrothed to Prince Vladimir of Novgorod, but was killed by his brother, Prince Yaropolk, in 1011.

modern_usage.modern_context: Inessa is a name of Slavic origin, derived from the name of the goddess Inara. It is a rare name in modern usage, and is primarily found in genealogy websites related to Slavic and Eastern European history.
